page: The Vultr voc-s-24c-192gb-3840s-amd is a memory-optimized and storage-rich instance within the Optimized Cloud Compute family. It features 24 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs derived from 12 physical cores on an AMD EPYC processor running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz, supporting simultaneous multithreading. Memory provisioning is substantial at 192.0 GB of RAM, establishing an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Local storage consists of a 3840 GB NVMe SSD, and the configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address without integrated GPU acceleration.

Benchmark evaluations reveal exceptional throughput in uncached memory bandwidth, reaching 458.63 GB/sec in large-block read operations and 223.24 GB/sec in large-block writes, placing the instance in the top 10 percent of evaluated systems. Compute execution is also strong, with PassMark CPU (51,919.27) and multi-core stress-ng (67,368.14) ranking in the top quartile. General single-core and application benchmarks, including Geekbench single-core (1,341.0), Geekbench multi-core (11,893.0), and Redis SET throughput (54.61 million operations per second), reflect middle-tier execution profiles consistent with the 2.0 GHz clock frequency.

Hardware tradeoffs center around the balance between memory capacity and vector acceleration. While the CPU supports standard AVX, AES-NI, and SHA extensions, it lacks AVX-512 and AMX instructions, limiting its utility for dense matrix operations and large-scale model inference. However, the qualitative cost efficiency of this configuration is favorable for workloads that demand high density per node, pairing massive memory capacity and 3.8 TB of fast local NVMe storage without requiring distributed storage attachments.

The instance is suited for memory-intensive production databases, large in-memory caching layers such as Redis or Memcached clusters, data transformation pipelines, and high-volume analytical workloads requiring fast local scratch disks.
description: The Vultr voc-s-24c-192gb-3840s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance engineered for memory-intensive and storage-heavy workloads. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor operating at 2.0 GHz, it supplies 24 dedicated vCPUs across 12 physical cores, 192.0 GB of system memory, and a bundled 3840 GB local NVMe SSD without GPU hardware. Benchmark results demonstrate top-decile uncached memory bandwidth exceeding 458 GB/sec read and 223 GB/sec write throughput, alongside top-quartile PassMark CPU scores. Single-thread execution and web serving benchmarks align with median performance levels due to standard clock frequencies. Lacking AVX-512 extensions, it is less suited for deep vector computation, but its high memory-to-core density and local NVMe capacity offer efficient utilization for in-memory databases, Redis caches, and data warehousing pipelines.
